annotation.cut_point:
We are given the identity:

$$
(x^2 + 1)(2x + 1)^{11} = a_0 + a_1(x+2) + a_2(x+2)^2 + \cdots + a_{13}(x+2)^{13}
$$

We are to find:

$$
a_0 + a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_{13}
$$

---

### Step 1: Understand the meaning of the sum

The expression on the right is a polynomial in terms of $(x+2)$, and the sum $a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{13}$ is the **value of the polynomial when $x = -2$**.

verified_state: Goal is to compute a_0 + a_1 + ... + a_{13}
The right-hand side is a polynomial expressed in powers of (x+2)
reflection.error_step: The expression on the right is a polynomial in terms of $(x+2)$, and the sum $a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{13}$ is the **value of the polynomial when $x = -2$**.
reflection.error_reason: Substituting x=-2 gives x+2=0, so the RHS becomes a_0 only, not the sum of all coefficients.
reflection.new_direction: Set x+2=1, i.e. x=-1, so that the RHS becomes a_0+a_1+...+a_{13}.
